independence_scope: intra-mesh Anthropic-family; agreement is corroboration, never cross-provider evidence

reviews.reasoning: Span re-derived against both witnesses. Ps 66 is an identity psalm (web_mt_offset_map psalms['66'] = rule identity, 20 WEB / 20 MT verses, mt_title_verses []), so web:Ps.66.1-web:Ps.66.4 = oshb:Ps.66.1-oshb:Ps.66.4 and no dual-cite obligation arises; ps_lib.web_to_mt(66,v) returned (66,v) for every verse I checked. The device_notes title claim is exact rather than approximate: psalm_device_inventory superscriptions['66'] gives labels mizmor, shir, lamnatseach and mt_title_verses 'prefix_of_v1', matching the row's statement that MT holds the title as the prefix of 66:1 rather than a counted verse, and verse_map_oshb Ps.66.1 carries no is_counted_title flag. No Davidic token and no historical note stand in the title bytes, so the three-label list is complete for this psalm. The Selah close is real: pmarks selah carries Ps.66.4 and WEB 66:4 ends “Selah.” The quoted second-person speech claim for web:Ps.66.3-web:Ps.66.4 holds at byte tier — MT 66:3 carries 2ms suffixes on מַעֲשֶׂ֑יךָ, עֻ֝זְּךָ֗ and אֹיְבֶֽיךָ. The rejected_alternative is sound and byte-backed: MT 66:5 opens לְכ֣וּ וּ֭רְאוּ, a genuine 2mp imperative pair one verse past the proposed extension. All 51 curly-quoted WEB strings in this cluster pass check_web_quotes (0 flags, GREEN), this row's included. The single defect is a count-object mismatch in the first substrate signal; it does not touch the span, which I would keep.

challenges.claim: The signal's label 'Imperative doublet' undercounts the chain it cites: the span web:Ps.66.1-web:Ps.66.2 carries three imperative tokens, not two, and the chain runs on into web:Ps.66.3.
challenges.evidence: Tokens spliced from verse_map_oshb and collated at byte tier against their own refs (Ps 66 identity numbering, so oshb v = web v): הָרִ֥יעוּ (oshb:Ps.66.1), זַמְּר֥וּ and שִׂ֥ימוּ (oshb:Ps.66.2), אִמְר֣וּ (oshb:Ps.66.3) — 4 imperative tokens across 3 verses, of which 3 fall inside the cited span web:Ps.66.1-web:Ps.66.2; unit = imperative tokens. Both witnesses agree on three in that span: “Make a joyful shout to God, all the earth!” (web:Ps.66.1) supplies one and “Sing to the glory of his name! Offer glory and praise!” (web:Ps.66.2) supplies two. The row's own rationale quotes all three clauses, so the content is present and only the count-label is wrong.

reviews.reasoning: The K/Q disclosure is this row's notable feature and it verifies exactly: pmarks kq holds one entry for this psalm, at Ps.66.7, and the MT bytes show the unpointed ketiv standing beside the pointed qere inside מֹ֘שֵׁ֤ל בִּגְבוּרָת֨וֹ עוֹלָ֗ם עֵ֭ינָיו בַּגּוֹיִ֣ם תִּצְפֶּ֑ינָה הַסּוֹרְרִ֓ים אַל ירימו יָר֖וּמוּ לָ֣מוֹ סֶֽלָה. The row discloses the note and states it is not engaged by the English-level warrant, which is correct — the warrant rests on WEB 66:7's opening clause “He rules by his might forever.” while the K/Q pair sits in the later clause about the rebellious. Because Ps 66 is an identity psalm the row's 'MT Ps.66.7 (web:Ps.66.7)' pairing is arithmetically right. Selah handling is span-scoped and symmetric: pmarks selah for this psalm = Ps.66.4, Ps.66.7, Ps.66.15; the row cites 66:4 as its front seam and 66:7 as its own close and makes no absence claim. Both opening imperatives splice byte-true at oshb:Ps.66.5 (לְכ֣וּ, וּ֭רְאוּ). WEB quotes verbatim per check_web_quotes. The rejected_alternative is answered on the right ground — 66:7 runs to its own Selah rather than opening a fresh address. No cross-tradition material is smuggled in: the exodus remark is prose about MT הָ֤פַךְ יָ֨ם, not a citation of any non-MT witness. Observation, not a defect: MT 66:6 closes נִשְׂמְחָה (byte tier), a 1cp form, so the community voice that later strophes lean on already surfaces inside this span; the row does not claim otherwise.

The opening driver is sound at byte tier: MT 66:8 opens בָּרְכ֖וּ and carries וְ֝הַשְׁמִ֗יעוּ, a genuine 2mp imperative pair, with the addressee named in the same verse, so the redirection the row describes is real. The closing seam is the row's true load-bearer and it is byte-confirmed on both sides: 1cp forms run unbroken through MT 66:8-12 (אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ 66:8; נַ֭פְשֵׁנוּ, רַגְלֵֽנוּ 66:9; בְחַנְתָּ֥נוּ, צְ֝רַפְתָּ֗נוּ 66:10; הֲבֵאתָ֥נוּ, בְמָתְנֵֽינוּ 66:11; לְרֹ֫אשֵׁ֥נוּ, בָּֽאנוּ, וַ֝תּוֹצִיאֵ֗נוּ 66:12) and give way to 1cs at MT 66:13 (אָב֣וֹא, אֲשַׁלֵּ֖ם, נְדָרָֽי). Selah handling is clean — pmarks places no selah inside 66:8-12 and the row claims none. Quotes verbatim. Observation, not a defect: the plural voice is not exclusive to 66:8-12, since MT 66:6 already closes נִשְׂמְחָה (byte tier); this does not damage either seam, because the row's opening rests on the imperative and its close on the we-to-I turn, and a verse of third-person material at 66:7 separates the two plural runs. The defect I file is an ordinal, and the span stands.

challenges.claim: The ordinal in 'A second imperative redirects the address' is wrong on either counting object available: MT 66:8's imperative is the third strophe-opening imperative in the psalm and the seventh imperative token.
challenges.evidence: Imperative tokens spliced from verse_map_oshb, each collated byte tier at its own ref (Ps 66 identity, oshb v = web v): הָרִ֥יעוּ (66:1), זַמְּר֥וּ and שִׂ֥ימוּ (66:2), אִמְר֣וּ (66:3), לְכ֣וּ and וּ֭רְאוּ (66:5), בָּרְכ֖וּ and וְ֝הַשְׁמִ֗יעוּ (66:8), לְכֽוּ and שִׁמְע֣וּ (66:16) = 10 imperative tokens across 6 verses; unit = imperative tokens. בָּרְכ֖וּ is token 7 of 10. Counting only the strophe-opening imperatives as this psalm is segmented here — 66:1, 66:5, 66:8, 66:16 — it is the third of 4, not the second. Both witnesses agree on the census: WEB reads “Come, and see” (web:Ps.66.5) before “Praise our God, you peoples!” (web:Ps.66.8).

reviews.reasoning: The row's driver is the we-to-I turn and it falls exactly where the row places it, byte-confirmed on both sides of the seam: MT 66:12 closes on 1cp forms (לְרֹ֫אשֵׁ֥נוּ, בָּֽאנוּ, וַ֝תּוֹצִיאֵ֗נוּ) and MT 66:13 opens 1cs (אָב֣וֹא, אֲשַׁלֵּ֖ם, נְדָרָֽי), every token spliced from verse_map_oshb at byte tier. Ps 66 is identity numbering, so the bare web: refs need no dual-cite and citation_sweep returns no problem on this row. The Selah close verifies against pmarks (Ps.66.15) and WEB 66:15 ends “Selah.” The rejected_alternative is grounded on the right fact — web:Ps.66.12's pronoun set is plural and belongs to the community report. Quotes verbatim per check_web_quotes. Two observations, neither a defect: WEB renders בֵיתְךָ֣ at MT 66:13 as “your temple” (web:Ps.66.13) where the noun is 'house', but the row's argument leans on the pronoun turn rather than on that rendering; and that same token carries a 2ms suffix, so address to God continues inside the vow — the row confines its claim to the first-person pronoun set and so does not overclaim a full addressee change. Confidence high is calibrated here: the seam has an independent byte-level warrant on both sides plus a Selah at the close.

The opening imperatives splice byte-true at oshb:Ps.66.16 (לְכֽוּ, שִׁמְע֣וּ), and the row's claim that this reopens the vocative register carried at web:Ps.66.5 is stronger in the original than the row states it: MT 66:5 and MT 66:16 share the identical opening token לְכ֣וּ / לְכֽוּ, differing only in accent, so the register link the row argues in English is corroborated at the consonantal level. The benediction-versus-doxology disclosure is the row's most checkable claim and it holds: psalm_device_inventory book_boundary_doxologies keys are Ps.41.14, Ps.72.18, Ps.72.19, Ps.89.53 and Ps.106.48, each recorded baruch true with amen counts 2/0/2/2/1, and Ps.66.20 is not among them; MT 66:20 opens בָּר֥וּךְ אֱלֹהִ֑ים and carries no amen token in its bytes. five_books places this psalm inside Book II (42-72), whose boundary doxology stands at 72:18-19, so the contrast the row draws is correct and is a real disclosure rather than decoration. Selah: pmarks gives Ps.66.15 as the front seam the row cites and places none inside 66:16-20; the row claims none. The first-person singular voice runs unbroken through the span in the MT bytes, so the continuity claim is right. Quotes verbatim per check_web_quotes.

Numbering is right throughout and I could not fault the arithmetic: web_mt_offset_map psalms['67'] = rule shift, k 1, 7 WEB / 8 MT verses, mt_title_verses [1]; ps_lib returns web 67:1 to MT 67:2, 67:2 to 67:3, 67:3 to 67:4, 67:5 to 67:6, and verse_map_oshb Ps.67.1 carries is_counted_title true, so every dual-cite in the refs array checks out and the title pseudo-ref form is the owner-ruled one. The Selah citation web:Ps.67.1 = oshb:Ps.67.2 matches pmarks, whose selah set for this psalm is exactly Ps.67.2 and Ps.67.5. The Elohistic figure is exact and its attribution is honest: psalm_device_inventory yhwh_elohim_per_psalm['67'] = yhwh 0, elohim 5, and I re-derived 5 unsuffixed tokens from the MT bytes (67:2, 67:4, 67:6, 67:7, 67:8) with the suffixed אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ at MT 67:7 correctly excluded, plus 0 YHWH. So the row is clean on numbering, marks and counts. Its structural warrant, however, fails on two independent grounds, and a third defect is machine-confirmed. I would keep the span — a three-verse opening movement closing on the refrain is defensible on refrain-lattice grounds — but the stated grounds for rejecting the rival seam are contradicted by the bytes, and a replacement warrant has to pass the test that kills this one.

challenges.claim: The signal's claim that second-person address to God runs web:Ps.67.1-web:Ps.67.2 is false at web:Ps.67.1, and the rejected_alternative's ground that no addressee shift separates web:Ps.67.1 from web:Ps.67.2 is contradicted by the bytes — the person shift falls precisely at that seam.
challenges.evidence: web:Ps.67.1 = oshb:Ps.67.2 under shift+1. MT 67:2 speaks of God in the third person throughout: יְחָנֵּ֥נוּ, וִֽיבָרְכֵ֑נוּ and יָ֤אֵ֥ר are prefix-conjugation forms governed by the subject in the same verse, and the face is פָּנָ֖יו — a 3ms suffix, 'his face' — all four tokens spliced from verse_map_oshb and collated byte tier at oshb:Ps.67.2. Token census over everything preceding the disputed seam, unit = word tokens as the extract serialises them: oshb:Ps.67.1 (the title) holds 4 tokens and oshb:Ps.67.2 holds 7, and across those 11 tokens the count bearing a 2ms pronominal suffix is 0 — the suffixes actually present in oshb:Ps.67.2 are 1cp on יְחָנֵּ֥נוּ, וִֽיבָרְכֵ֑נוּ and אִתָּ֣נוּ, and 3ms on פָּנָ֖יו. The first 2ms address-forms in the psalm are the 2 at web:Ps.67.2 = oshb:Ps.67.3: דַּרְכֶּ֑ךָ and יְשׁוּעָתֶֽךָ, both byte tier at oshb:Ps.67.3, out of that verse's 6 tokens. WEB agrees with MT here, so this is not a rendering artifact: “May God be merciful to us, bless us, and cause his face to shine on us.” (web:Ps.67.1) speaks about God, while “That your way may be known on earth, and your salvation among all nations,” (web:Ps.67.2) speaks to God. Of the three items the signal offers, 'your way' and 'your salvation' are second-person and both sit in web:Ps.67.2; the only item anchoring the claim to web:Ps.67.1 is 'bless us', which is a third-person form with a 1cp object. The addressee shift the rejected_alternative denies is therefore the strongest tier-1 warrant for the very seam it dismisses.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative deploys the Selah as counterevidence against a seam the Selah actually sits on, and asserts a corroborating close at web:Ps.67.3 where the inventory records no Selah at all.
challenges.evidence: pmarks selah carries 2 loci for this psalm, Ps.67.2 and Ps.67.5 (MT keys), i.e. web:Ps.67.1 and web:Ps.67.4 under shift+1, one occurrence each; unit = selah-bearing verses. WEB 67:1 ends “Selah.” — the mark closes web:Ps.67.1, which is exactly the seam the rejected_alternative rejects, and the row's own first signal concedes the mark is 'interior to this row rather than at its edge'. There is no selah at oshb:Ps.67.4 = web:Ps.67.3, so the assertion that the Selah 'corroborates a close after the refrain at web:Ps.67.3' has no inventory support in either direction. Span-scoped: the only selah inside web:Ps.67.1-web:Ps.67.3 is the one at web:Ps.67.1. Selah is corroboration only and never a driver, but here the corroboration runs against the row rather than for it, so it cannot serve as the ground of rejection.

challenges.claim: web:Ps.67.4 is argued in the rationale but never mirrored in boundary_evidence_refs, and the gap is masked by a numbering collision with the oshb:Ps.67.4 entry that is present.
challenges.evidence: check_refs_mirror.py reports for this row argued_but_unmirrored: ['Ps.67.4'], the only flag it raises across the cluster (8 rows checked, flag_count 1, status FLAGS). The rationale argues that the strophe at web:Ps.67.4-web:Ps.67.5 repeats this movement, and web:Ps.67.4 lies outside this row's span web:Ps.67.1-web:Ps.67.3, so it must be mirrored. The refs array does carry an oshb:Ps.67.4 token, but under shift+1 oshb:Ps.67.4 = web:Ps.67.3 — a different verse from web:Ps.67.4, which is oshb:Ps.67.5. The missing entry is web:Ps.67.4 = oshb:Ps.67.5; the present entry cannot discharge it.

challenges.claim: The device_notes title-label list is incomplete for this psalm: the inventory records four labels where the row states three, and the omitted one is the label that distinguishes this superscription.
challenges.evidence: psalm_device_inventory superscriptions['67'] gives 4 labels — mizmor, shir, lamnatseach and binginot — where the row states the first 3 only. The omitted label is byte-present in the title verse as בִּנְגִינֹ֗ת, word index 1 of oshb:Ps.67.1 (title = MT v1 under shift+1, hence web:Ps.67.0 = oshb:Ps.67.1). It is not an incidental word but a tracked label class: genre_label_membership['binginot'] = [4, 6, 54, 55, 61, 67, 76], 7 psalms with this one among them; unit = psalms carrying the label. It is also precisely what separates this superscription from the 3-label set the same inventory records at superscriptions['66'] = mizmor, shir, lamnatseach, all 3 of which the two titles share. ngram7 shows the seven-gram 'title carries mizmor shir and lamnatseach labels' recurring across 2 rows in this cluster (gate 10, status GREEN, so not itself a templating failure), which is how a label list correct for one psalm reaches a psalm whose set is larger.

reviews.reasoning: The one row in the cluster carrying original-language quotation, and every claim in it re-derived clean. The refrain quote יוֹד֖וּךָ עַמִּ֥ים אֱלֹהִ֑ים י֝וֹד֗וּךָ עַמִּ֥ים כֻּלָּֽם collates at byte tier — the only quotation-grade tier — at both cited refs, oshb:Ps.67.4 and oshb:Ps.67.6, and a direct comparison of the two source strings shows them equal at every tier (57 codepoints each, zero differing positions), so the byte-identity claim is exact and not merely approximate; I had expected an accentual divergence between the two occurrences and there is none in this extract. Dual-cites are arithmetically right under shift+1 (oshb:Ps.67.4 = web:Ps.67.3, oshb:Ps.67.6 = web:Ps.67.5), and the out-of-span anchor web:Ps.67.3 is properly mirrored in boundary_evidence_refs — check_refs_mirror raises nothing on this row. The Selah claim matches pmarks (Ps.67.5 = web:Ps.67.4). The row is scrupulous exactly where overclaiming would be easy: it says the refrain 'repeats in English' at web:Ps.67.3 and web:Ps.67.5 'with sentence-initial capitalization as the difference', and that is right to the letter — “let the peoples praise you, God. Let all the peoples praise you.” (web:Ps.67.3) continues the clause from the preceding verse in lower case against “Let the peoples praise you, God. Let all the peoples praise you.” (web:Ps.67.5), the sole difference being the initial letter. citation_sweep returns two prose_dual_warns here for oshb refs standing beside Hebrew without in-field WEB arithmetic, but the tool itself classes these as an author-wave enhancement with the pairing living in refs and returns status GREEN with an empty problems list, so I do not file them. No selah, paseq, inverted-nun or suspended claim is made beyond what the inventories carry.

The span is right and survives the challenges below: the refrain returns at web:Ps.67.5 = oshb:Ps.67.6 and does not return again, so the closing couplet web:Ps.67.6-web:Ps.67.7 = oshb:Ps.67.7-oshb:Ps.67.8 is a genuine unit, and the row's second driver — that the peoples-praise line is not repeated here — is true and tier-1. The row makes no original-language citation and its refs are bare web: throughout, which the convention permits, so no dual-cite obligation arises and citation_sweep returns no problem on it; WEB quotes are verbatim. What fails is the row's lead driver, a mood contrast that does not exist in the original: both halves of it come apart against the pointed bytes. Note also that the psalm is jussive-driven where the adjacent psalm in this cluster is imperative-driven, so the vocabulary carried across does not fit this text. Confidence high is over-calibrated while the lead driver stands as written, though the refrain-non-return warrant alone would support a lower-confidence keep.

challenges.claim: The refrain is not imperative: the row labels the refrain verb an imperative when it is a prefix-conjugation third-person plural form with a 2ms suffix whose subject is the peoples, and the imperative of that root is a he-prefix form the inventory records elsewhere in the book.
challenges.evidence: The refrain verb יוֹד֖וּךָ is spliced from verse_map_oshb and collates byte tier at oshb:Ps.67.4; the subject standing beside it in the same colon is עַמִּ֥ים, so the peoples are the grammatical subject in the third person rather than an addressed second person, and the 2ms element in the form is the object suffix. The 2mp imperative of that root is he-prefixed and is attested at the loci psalm_device_inventory records as hodu_openings — Ps.33.2, Ps.105.1, Ps.107.1, Ps.118.1, Ps.118.29, Ps.136.1 — of which I spliced הוֹד֣וּ (oshb:Ps.105.1) and the defectively spelled הֹד֣וּ (oshb:Ps.107.1), both byte tier; the contrast with the refrain form is visible in the first consonant. sweep.py --skel over the refrain verb's skeleton returns count_unit verses, 5 verses (MT Ps.67.4, Ps.67.6, Ps.88.11, Ps.138.4, Ps.145.10) and 7 token occurrences, and no occurrence of the form is imperative. WEB renders it as a jussive, “Let the peoples praise you, God.” (web:Ps.67.5), not as an imperative addressed to the peoples.

challenges.claim: The declarative-replaces-volitive contrast that opens the row is an artifact of the WEB rendering: in MT the closing couplet carries the same prefix conjugation as the refrain it is contrasted with, leaving the contrast one token deep.
challenges.evidence: The closing couplet's finite verbs, all spliced from verse_map_oshb and collated byte tier at their own refs: נָתְנָ֣ה and יְ֝בָרְכֵ֗נוּ (oshb:Ps.67.7), יְבָרְכֵ֥נוּ and וְיִֽירְא֥וּ (oshb:Ps.67.8). Three of those four are prefix-conjugation forms, the same conjugation class as the refrain's יוֹד֖וּךָ (oshb:Ps.67.4, byte tier); only נָתְנָ֣ה is a suffix-conjugation form. Across the whole psalm I count 15 finite verb tokens in the MT bytes, of which 14 are prefix-conjugation and exactly 1 (נָתְנָ֣ה, oshb:Ps.67.7) is suffix-conjugation, with 0 imperatives; unit = finite verb tokens. The mood difference the row cites is visible only in WEB's choice to render “The earth has yielded its increase. God, even our own God, will bless us.” (web:Ps.67.6) against “Let the peoples praise you, God. Let all the peoples praise you.” (web:Ps.67.5) — a single-witness rendering distinction, not a tier-1 signal in the original, and the seam needs a warrant that does not depend on it. The staged extract carries no morphology layer, so this is argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings, as the toolkit directs.
